svg.text: Chief Market Cat - Phased Build Roadmap
Build like CSC: deterministic pipeline first, evidence and risk gates second, supervised trading only after proof.
Phase 0 - Foundation
Define markets, assets, timeframes, risk rules and schemas.
Outputs: scope, source list, MarketItem, SignalItem, TradeMemo.
PINNED MVP 1 - Market Intelligence Brief
Fetch market/news/macro data, normalize, classify signals, brief.
No live trading. No execution. Decision support only.
PINNED DAY 2 - Evidence + Risk Gates
Add evidence_state, verify_signal, risk_guardian and review queue.
Weak high-impact signals are held. Trade ideas become paper candidates only.
Phase 3 - Paper Trading
Connect broker sandbox and generate human-approved trade memos.
Track entries, exits, P&L, mistakes and process quality.
Phase 4 - Portfolio Layer
Add exposure, correlation, concentration, drawdown and cash checks.
Watchlist ranking becomes opportunity adjusted for portfolio risk.
Phase 5 - Permissioned Live Execution
Broker gate, human approval, small size, strict max loss, kill switch.
Live trading remains revocable and audited.
Phase 6 - Blue-Sky Multi-Agent System
Specialist agents coordinate, simulate scenarios and evaluate regimes.
Automation is narrow, supervised and reversible.
MVP 1 Scope
Goal: know what matters in global markets today.
Outputs: regime, risk tone, top moves, top signals, held items.
Excludes: autonomous trading, leverage calls, options execution.
Success: useful brief with traceable evidence and no false urgency.
Day 2 Scope
Goal: prevent weak evidence and bad risk from becoming trades.
Build: evidence_state, verify_signal, risk_gate, review queue.
Outputs: passed signals, held signals, paper-trade candidates.
Excludes: live execution and complex orchestration.
Success: every candidate has invalidation and risk boundary.
Build Principle
Do not build an AI trader first.
Build an evidence-aware market monitor, then a paper-trade
decision system, then permissioned execution.
Risk Guardian gets veto power before broker execution.
